title: The Ending & the Moral
text: 'Orwell creates a shocking and unexpected ending to Animal Farm.' How far do you agree with this statement? Write about: what happens towards the end of the novel, and how Orwell presents the ending.

Top band (26–30 marks + up to 4 spelling/grammar)Critical, exploratory response. Students should argue BOTH sides. The ending IS shocking: the image of pigs walking on hind legs, carrying whips, and drinking with humans is viscerally disturbing. The final line ('impossible to say which was which') delivers a powerful emotional punch. HOWEVER, the ending is arguably NOT unexpected — Orwell foreshadows it throughout: the pigs take the milk (Ch.2), move into the farmhouse (Ch.6), walk upright is foreshadowed by the gradual humanisation of the pigs. The fable structure means the moral is inevitable. The real shock is how completely the revolution has failed — the farm is worse than under Jones ('the lower animals did more work and received less food'). Context: Orwell is critiquing Stalinism specifically — the ending mirrors how the USSR under Stalin became as oppressive as the Tsarist regime it replaced.
